description.value: Whole-brain voxel-based morphometry study of gray matter volume in male adolescents with antisocial substance dependence compared with controls, including regressions with impulsivity and substance dependence severity.

spans.text: we performed whole-brain voxel based morphometry (VBM) to examine prefrontal gray matter volume in male adolescents with ASD as compared to controls.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional comparison of male adolescent ASD patients and controls.

spans.text: The whole-brain analyses compared volume estimates between groups using analyses of covariance (ANCOVA).

value: Compared to controls, ASD adolescents had smaller gray matter volume in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex/inferior frontal junction, right lingual gyrus, and bilateral cerebellum. These regions are relevant to cognitive control, inhibition, empathy, and behavioral regulation.

spans.text: Thus compared to controls, our patients had less GM volume in areas relevant to behavioral inhibition, impulsivity, and empathy toward others, and more GM volume in areas involved in self-referential processing.

The total scan time for structural acquisition was 9 min 12 s.
Subjects were scanned in a 3 T MR scanner (General Electric) using a standard quadrature head coil.
